title: Cofactor maps are natural for derived isomorphisms of two-term projective complexes
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring. Let $E=[P\xrightarrow{u}Q]$ be a complex in degrees $-1,0$ of finite projective $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], with ranks $c,c+1$ at every prime, where $c\geq0$. Put $D(E)=(\bigwedge^c P)^\vee\otimes_A\bigwedge^{c+1}Q$, where $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(V,A)$ and exterior powers are [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. Define $w_E:\operatorname{coker}(u)\to D(E)$ by the following local formula: for a basis $p_1,\ldots,p_c$ of $P$ and a lift $v\in Q$ of $\bar v\in\operatorname{coker}(u)$, its value is $(p_1\wedge\cdots\wedge p_c)^\vee\otimes(u(p_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u(p_c)\wedge v)$. This formula is independent of the basis and lift and defines an $A$-linear map. Let $E'=[P'\to Q']$ be another such complex, of ranks $c',c'+1$, and let $a:E\xrightarrow{\sim}E'$ be an isomorphism in the derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the determinant comparison $D(a):D(E)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(E')$ of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, normalized affine locally by the kernel-first exact-sequence construction: for a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism, use bases of the kernel followed by lifts of bases of the quotient in both degrees, and trivialize the determinant of the acyclic kernel by its differential. Then $D(a)\circ w_E=w_{E'}\circ H^0(a)$, with $H^0(E)=\operatorname{coker}(u)$ and $H^0(E')=\operatorname{coker}(u')$. No injectivity of $u$ or $u'$, and no regularity or reducedness of $A$, is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-cofactor-local-descent] to $u$ and $u'$. Its unique maps have exactly the stipulated local formula, so these are $w_E,w_{E'}$, including basis/lift independence and linearity. It also supplies the localization identifications used below.

proof.text: Now let $a:E\xrightarrow{\sim}E'$ be the given derived isomorphism. Both complexes are bounded above with projective terms, hence K-projective by the bounded-projective theorem. The K-projective Hom bijection represents $a$ by a chain map $f:E\to E'$. Since cohomology factors through the derived category and $a$ is invertible, every $H^i(f)$ is an isomorphism; thus $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism. These statements use the ordinary derived category of modules, with no restriction on the ring or on the kernels of $u,u'$.

source.place: Tag 064B (lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex); K-projectivity and the Hom bijection supplied by the two cited Mathlib leaves.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-good-two-term-surjective-diagrams] to this chain quasi-isomorphism $f$. Choose a finite free surjection $\pi:F=A^n\to P'$. The cited statement gives $M=[P\oplus F\xrightarrow{u\oplus1}Q\oplus F]$ and degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphisms $b:M\to E$, $t:M\to E'$ with $t\simeq fb$. Consequently $t=ab$ in the derived category. The ranks of $M$ are $c+n,c+n+1$; thus the construction of step 1 also gives $w_M$.

Apply [lem-sfb-surjective-cofactor-compatibility] to $b$ and $t$: it gives $T_bw_M=w_EH^0(b)$ and $T_tw_M=w_{E'}H^0(t)$. The normalization fixed in the statement identifies $T_b=D(b)$ and $T_t=D(t)$. Determinant functoriality gives $D(t)=D(a)D(b)$; cohomology functoriality gives $H^0(t)=H^0(a)H^0(b)$. Therefore $D(a)w_EH^0(b)=D(t)w_M=w_{E'}H^0(a)H^0(b)$. Since $H^0(b)$ is invertible, cancel it on the right to obtain $D(a)w_E=w_{E'}H^0(a)$.
